html:
A canal of about 240 kilometres across southern France, from Toulouse to the Mediterranean, built from 1666 to 1681. With the Garonne River it links the Atlantic to the Mediterranean, so boats need not sail around Spain.

The man behind it was Pierre-Paul Riquet, a tax collector in Languedoc with no training as an engineer. His key idea was how to feed water to the highest point of the route: he gathered streams from the Montagne Noire hills into a large reservoir and channels. Louis XIV and his minister Colbert backed the work, and Riquet put much of his own fortune into it. About 12,000 workers dug it, and Riquet died months before it opened.

It has dozens of locks, aqueducts and one of the first canal tunnels. It was one of the largest building works of its century in Europe and helped trade in wine and grain. Railways later took most of its traffic. Today it is lined with plane trees, used by holiday boats, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
sum: A canal of about 240 kilometres across southern France, from Toulouse to the Mediterranean, built from 1666 to 1681. With the Garonne River it links the Atlantic to the Mediterranean, so boats need not sail around Spain.
